title: RFK Jr. may upend how vaccine recommendations are categorized
gist: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has issued a 10-page Request for Information, published in the Federal Register on Monday with a September 20 comment deadline, floating replacement of the CDC's three vaccine recommendation categories with softer designations such as 'recommended with qualification' or shared clinical decision-making. Reclassifying categories rather than withdrawing recommendations outright is a procedurally cleaner route than his earlier unilateral changes, which a federal judge has temporarily blocked as likely illegal.

insights.claim: The CDC currently grants three categories of vaccination recommendation — routine/universal, risk-based, and shared clinical decision-making — informed by the independent Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: These three tiers are the structure everything downstream keys off; changing the tier definitions changes outcomes without changing any individual vaccine's status.

insights.claim: Kennedy's RFI raises the possibility that vaccinations currently considered routine or universal could be given designations sounding less definitive or more conditional, such as 'recommended with qualification' or shared clinical decision-making.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: Softening the language rather than removing recommendations is the lower-friction path to reducing uptake — watch category wording, not vaccine-by-vaccine decisions.
insights.locator: Under anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

insights.claim: The RFI gives special consideration to shared clinical decision-making, currently used rarely — Meningococcal B is one of the few vaccines with it — describing it as an 'intermediate category' that 'provides no default' and avoids a binary between universal recommendation and none at all.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Promoting a rare category to a default is the specific proposed mechanism — a no-default recommendation is functionally a coverage and mandate downgrade.
insights.locator: As for what the new recommendation categories might be

insights.claim: The RFI floats additional undefined category options including 'recommended, but not during infancy,' 'recommended with qualification,' and 'shared clinical decision-making with qualification,' without elaborating what any of them would mean.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: Undefined categories preserve maximum administrative discretion later — the vagueness is the feature, and the definitions are the thing to watch for.
insights.quote: The document does not elaborate on what any of those categories might mean.
insights.locator: Otherwise, the RFI asks for other category options

insights.claim: The article notes the RFI itself acknowledges that shared clinical decision-making has raised confusion when used, even as it asks the public to weigh in on expanding its use.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The proposal concedes its own preferred category confuses providers — evidence the goal is ambiguity rather than clarity.
insights.locator: But it also notes that SCDM, when used, has raised confusion

insights.claim: A federal judge has temporarily blocked Kennedy's changes to federal vaccine recommendations, most of his ACIP appointments, and his reconstituted ACIP's changes, ruling in March that they were likely illegal and done without proper procedure amid a lawsuit led by the American Academy of Pediatrics.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The injunction is the operative constraint — the pediatric trade body, not Congress, is the effective check on HHS vaccine policy right now.
insights.locator: For now, a federal judge has temporarily blocked

insights.claim: The RFI appears to be an effort to follow administrative procedures, which often include public comment periods — implying the earlier procedural defeat is driving a shift to a slower but more litigation-resistant approach.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: Procedurally correct rulemaking is much harder to enjoin than unilateral action — expect this track to survive where the earlier one did not.
insights.quote: The RFI appears to be part of an effort to follow administrative procedures, which often include public comment periods.

insights.claim: Kennedy prefaces the RFI only by citing an executive order on vaccines that Trump signed two weeks earlier aimed at slashing and overhauling federal vaccine recommendations, and has made no new rules or recommendations for the categories yet.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: The executive order is the stated legal predicate — its scope determines how far the eventual rulemaking can reach.
insights.locator: In his RFI, Kennedy prefaces his efforts

insights.claim: The comment deadline for the 10-page RFI, posted online Friday and published in the Federal Register on Monday, is September 20.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: A hard, near-term date — September 20 is the checkpoint after which formal rulemaking on vaccine categories can proceed.
insights.quote: The deadline to comment on the questions and ideas is September 20.
insights.locator: However, he laid out ideas and possibilities

themes.theme: Evidentiary basis and the placebo-trial argument

insights.claim: Before Kennedy's oversight, the CDC and ACIP used an evidence-based decision-making framework to assign recommendation types, and there is no clear evidence-based reason to question the current categories nor any evidence supporting the ones Kennedy proposes.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: An evidentiary vacuum behind the proposed change is the vulnerability litigants will target in any arbitrary-and-capricious challenge.
insights.quote: There is no clear, evidence-based reason to question the current categories, nor any evidence to support changing to the new categories Kennedy proposes.
insights.locator: Before Kennedy’s oversight, the CDC and ACIP

insights.claim: The RFI seeks input on handling recommendations when randomized controlled trial evidence is 'absent, infeasible, or unethical to obtain,' which connects to Kennedy's recurring claim that childhood vaccine trials are flawed for not using inert placebos.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Codifying an RCT-evidence standard into the category framework would let a placebo-trial objection downgrade many existing vaccines at once.
insights.locator: It also seeks input on how to handle recommendations

insights.claim: Scientific and medical experts have largely dismissed the placebo-trial attack, noting such trials are unnecessary, in many cases unethical, and in some cases the claim is simply false.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The scientific consensus rejects the premise, so the fight moves to whether a procedurally valid rule can rest on a rejected premise.
insights.locator: Scientific and medical experts have largely dismissed

insights.claim: The RFI asks whether vaccine recommendations should be made with a 'presumption in favor of individual autonomy and religious freedom.'
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: Building an autonomy and religious-freedom presumption into federal recommendations would ripple directly into state school-mandate exemption law.
insights.quote: presumption in favor of individual autonomy and religious freedom
insights.locator: More specifically, the RFI asks the public

insights.claim: Kennedy previously tried to unilaterally slash the CDC's childhood vaccine recommendations to match Denmark's, a country the article describes as tiny, homogenous, with universal healthcare, and recommending fewer vaccines than any other high-income country.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Establishes the intended endpoint — the Denmark benchmark signals how far the eventual category rewrite is meant to go.
insights.locator: Kennedy previously tried to unilaterally slash

insights.claim: Kennedy fired all 17 experts on ACIP and repopulated the panel with hand-selected allies sharing his anti-vaccine beliefs, and the reconstituted panel dropped the universal recommendation for a birth dose of hepatitis B vaccine.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The hepatitis B birth-dose reversal is the concrete precedent for how a category change translates into an actual recommendation withdrawal.
insights.locator: Kennedy also fired all 17 experts on ACIP

insights.claim: HHS framed the RFI publicly as examining whether the current framework reflects strength of evidence, accounts for individual circumstances and values, and supports informed discussions among patients, parents, and providers.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Department of Health and Human Services
insights.so_what: The official framing is deliberately procedural and neutral — the gap between framing and prior actions is what a court would examine.
insights.quote: examining whether the current recommendation framework appropriately reflects the strength of the evidence, accounts for individual circumstances and values
